title: Put a blood-pressure cuff on a training arm: wrap it round, close the hook-and-loop, inflate it and start the monitor
keywords: wrapping a flexible band round a limb
instruction: Put the blood-pressure cuff on the arm, inflate it and start the monitor.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, about 1.4M US workers), medical assistants (31-9092.00, about 0.8M) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061.00, about 0.6M) all list measuring and recording vital signs, blood pressure among them, as a core task, done many times a shift. Every reading starts with fitting the cuff: a floppy 52 cm band has to be carried round the upper arm with one hand while the other brings the hook end over it and presses the hook-and-loop closed, with the lower edge 2 to 3 cm above the elbow crease. Only then is the monitor inflated and started, and the cuff is left alone while it reads.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left, z up from the table top). The arm: a life-size male display-mannequin left arm (rigid PVC, skin colour), held straight out along x on the midline, palm up, thumb to the left. Its cut shoulder end is screwed to a wooden block (x -3 to 3, y -6 to 6, 10.8 cm tall). The upper arm runs from the shoulder end at x 3 to the elbow crease at x 33 (a darker line across the top), its axis 5.8 cm above the table; it is 31 cm round at the shoulder end, 28 cm round 10 cm above the crease and 26 cm round at the crease, and 0.9 to 1.7 cm clear of the table all along. The forearm (25 cm to the wrist) and the hand lie on a grey foam pad (x 35 to 78, y -6.5 to 6.5, 1.8 cm thick). The cuff: an adult size 11 reusable blood-pressure cuff (Welch Allyn FlexiPort REUSE-11, for arms 25 to 34 cm round), navy nylon, 52 x 14.5 cm, 3 mm thick, 91 g, lying open on the table under the upper arm with its inner (skin) face up and its length across the arm: from y -27 (right end) to y 25 (left end), its width from x 13.25 to 27.75, so its lower edge is 5.25 cm above the elbow crease. The last 8 cm at each end stands curled up off the table, the curl of a cuff kept rolled up. Its bladder fills the 27 cm at the right end; a white artery arrow on the outer face marks the bladder's middle. The whole outer face is loop fabric; the last 12 cm of the inner face at the left end is the light-grey hook strip. A 1.5 cm grey tube leaves the cuff's lower edge 10 cm from its right end and joins the monitor's dark-grey hose (6 mm, 57 cm free), which runs forward to x 50, along to y -38 and back into the front face of the monitor. The monitor: an automatic upper-arm blood-pressure monitor, a light-grey box 14 cm (x) by 10 cm (y) by 5 cm tall, 450 g, lying on the table centred at x 27, y -42, its dark screen on top toward the front. Two round buttons on top, 2.2 cm across, standing 4 mm proud, 3 mm of travel, about 1.5 N to press: the green INFLATE button at x 23.5, y -39.5 and the blue START button at x 23.5, y -44.5. INFLATE pumps the cuff's bladder up to its holding pressure (2 s), which draws a closed cuff tight round the arm; START then takes the reading, which needs the cuff left alone for 2 s. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: a ruler, the trial video and the monitor's display. Closed: at least 8 of the hook strip's 12 cm is stuck to the cuff's loop face, and the cuff goes at least once round the upper arm, between its shoulder end and the elbow crease, with no part of it more than 7 cm off the skin. 0 if, at the end, the cuff is not round the upper arm like this (whatever else happened), or the monitor is knocked over (tilted over 30 degrees) or off the table. Otherwise, at the end: +0.40 closed; +0.20 the cuff's lower edge is 1.5 to 4 cm above the elbow crease all the way round; +0.20 inflated: INFLATE was pressed while the cuff was closed, and the inflated cuff now lies on the arm all round its closed loop (no part of it, up to the end of the stuck hook strip, more than 1.5 cm off the skin); +0.20 reading: START was pressed after that, with the cuff still closed, and no gripper touched the cuff during the 2 s that followed. INFLATE pressed before the cuff is closed does nothing (the monitor shows a cuff error), nor does START pressed before INFLATE. The hook strip sticks only where it is pressed flat onto the loop face, face to face, with at least 3 N. The trial ends with success once 1.0 has held for 2 s.
reset_notes: Peel the hook strip off, let the cuff down and open it, roll each end up for a minute so it curls, and lay the cuff flat at its marks under the arm, inner face up, hook strip on the left. Coil the hose back along its path. Put the monitor back at its marks and clear its display.
fidelity: Rigid-body sim. The cuff is 13 rigid 4 cm strips on sprung hinges; its curled ends are springs. Hook-and-loop is a rule: a hook strip pressed flat on the loop face with at least 3 N is held where it lies. The bladder's inflation is a rule: with the cuff closed, INFLATE makes the 7 joints inside the bladder close up along the band (up to 2 cm each, at most 5 N), so the cuff draws onto the arm. The reading is START, then 2 s untouched.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused the instruction before acting, nothing scored; demo: 1.0
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 refused the instruction before the arms moved, so there is no run video.
